champion_baseline.name: Model 1 Experiment 3 Variant 3 (Functional Layout Density)
champion_baseline.architecture: Equal-weight XGBoost + LightGBM + CatBoost in log-price space
champion_baseline.features: Experiment 2 Baseline (81 features) + BathToBedRatio + SF_Per_Bedroom = 83 features

leakage_analysis.mechanism: Gradient boosted trees achieve high in-sample R2 (> 0.985) by learning fine-grained leaf partitions. When a meta-regressor is trained on in-sample base model predictions, it optimizes over memorized training errors rather than true out-of-sample generalization errors. This leads to severe multicollinear weight inflation (large positive and negative opposing weights), collapsing test performance.
leakage_analysis.historical_precedent: Experiment 1 Ridge Stacking demonstrated this exact failure mode, where unconstrained meta-weights resulted in wild out-of-distribution test extrapolations ($1,262,492 on test ID 2550).

stacking_architecture_specification.meta_training_generation: For each outer fold k in 1..5, base models are trained on 3 of the 4 inner folds and predict on the 4th inner fold, assembling completely held-out meta-training features for the outer training set.
stacking_architecture_specification.test_inference_generation: Each of the 5 outer folds trains base models on all outer training data (4/5 of dataset) and meta-models on inner OOF predictions. Test predictions are generated by passing test data through each fold's base models into that fold's meta-model, and averaging the 5 outer fold predictions in log-price space.

recommendation.outcome: Stacking is feasible but unlikely to justify its computational cost.
rationale: Individual base-model OOF predictions are fully verified and aligned in Experiment 4A artifacts.
Base model predictions are extremely collinear (r = 0.9896 to 0.9951), providing virtually no orthogonal signal.
The theoretical in-sample ceiling of a linear meta-learner on the 1,460 OOF matrix is a mere 0.00047 RMSLE improvement.
Realistic held-out 5-fold evaluation of a Ridge meta-model results in performance degradation (+0.00111 RMSLE, 0.12657 vs 0.12546).
Experiment 4A previously demonstrated that constrained blending yielded an insignificant delta of -0.00004 RMSLE.
Executing a true leakage-safe nested 5x4 CV requires 75 model fits, multiplying training time by 15x with near-zero likelihood of improving upon equal-weight averaging.
